title: MusePulse Lite: Implement Persistent Dark Mode Setting
description: This scenario evaluates an agent's ability to perform incremental feature development over multiple sessions. The agent is tasked with adding a persistent Dark Mode setting to the 'MusePulse Lite' application, a simple mobile utility for capturing daily thoughts. The task is broken into three sessions: updating the data model, creating the UI control, and implementing the visual change. This requires the agent to retain context between sessions, understand the project's architecture (Model-ViewModel-View), and modify multiple C files.

project_spec.name: MusePulse Lite
project_spec.description:
MusePulse Lite is a pocket-sized "creative trigger" utility that lets users capture micro-ideas (text, color, audio snippets) in under three seconds and instantly resurface them later when a matching creative mood is detected. Every interaction—tapping the record button, tilting the phone, receiving a push reminder—fires lightweight events that ripple through an Observer/MVVM graph written entirely in C.  

The app turns everyday phone gestures into stimulus: a quick shake snapshots the current screen palette, an incoming notification can open a previously saved "idea capsule," and a single tap shares it to social feeds. Local storage (SQLite) preserves capsules offline, while a tiny crash-reporting singleton guards stability. Despite its simplicity, MusePulse Lite showcases how an event-driven core can transform an ordinary note-taker into an inspiring, responsive companion for creators on the go.
dependencies: libuv – portable event loop (core observer dispatch & async I/O)
SDL2 – cross-platform input/gesture layer and responsive UI primitives
cURL + cJSON – REST bridge for push_notifications & social_sharing endpoints
Sentry-Native – lightweight crash_reporting client for C
nanovg – vector UI rendering for fluid layouts (responsive_ui)
